title: Signature-based, not count-based — semantic identity over raw cardinality
body: The diminishing-returns breaker compares finding IDENTITY (signature sets) across rounds, not cardinality. Reason: count-only is the wrong signal — operators legitimately volley 5–10x to improve a feature, and as the implementer fixes earlier findings the auditor often surfaces NEW findings of similar count. `[3, 3]` flat counts can mean 'same 3 problems unresolved' (legitimate trip) OR '3 different problems each round' (false-positive trip). Cardinality conflates these; signature equality distinguishes them. Why this is now the right move: F001 of plan 003 (nested-orchestration) introduced `compute_finding_signature` for the repeated-finding hard stop on parent chains, and `feedback_volley_failure_taxonomy.md` memory captured the same pattern at the operator level (raw count is misleading). The platform now has both the conceptual machinery and the empirical evidence to fix the breaker — exactly the demand-driven trigger discipline (D012/D013 of plan 003) at work. How to apply: any future heuristic that needs to detect 'same problem persisting' should reuse `compute_finding_signature` / `compute_audit_finding_signature` rather than count-based proxies. Cardinality is fine for budget/quota signals (count of operations); identity is required for semantic-convergence signals.

title: Severity is NOT part of the signature — downgraded findings keep the same identity
body: `compute_audit_finding_signature` derives signature from category + file:line locality + normalized issue text. Severity (e.g., 'high', 'medium', 'low', 'info') is intentionally EXCLUDED. Reason: an auditor downgrading a finding from high→medium between rounds is the SAME finding with a re-evaluated severity, not a different finding. If severity were in the signature, the implementer 'fixing' a finding via downgrade-pressure would change its signature and silently exit the persisted-set, breaking the convergence detection. The whole point of signature-based diminishing-returns is to detect when the auditor really IS stuck on the same issue regardless of how its severity is being framed. How to apply: signature semantics in this platform model 'is this the same problem' — they should not include fields that vary across observations of the same problem (severity, recommendation phrasing, evidence detail). Code+class+locality+issue text is the principled set.

title: Round-count threshold stays a constant; no operator config knob in v1
body: DIMINISHING_RETURNS_MIN_ROUNDS = 2 remains a module-level constant in circuit_breakers.py. No `~/.jarvis/quota_caps.json` knob, no env var, no per-project override. Reason: the COUNT-only heuristic was over-firing because it was the wrong signal, not because the threshold was too tight. With signature-based behavior in place, two rounds of the SAME unresolved finding signatures is a strong correctness signal — the breaker should fire then. If signature-based behavior turns out to over- or under-fire in practice, the right response is another small platform plan (move threshold to operator config, or change the convergence rule), not a knob added speculatively now. Adding the knob first would be the same 'treat the symptom' move D001 explicitly rejected. How to apply: resist adding operator config until you have evidence that operators legitimately disagree on the right value across projects. v1 ships with the principled default; v2-of-this-fix (if needed) adds the knob with that evidence in hand.

title: Fallback to count when signatures unavailable, name fallback in breaker reason
body: When ANY round in the convergence window has at least one finding whose `compute_audit_finding_signature` returns None (missing or whitespace-only `issue` text), the breaker falls back to the legacy non-decreasing-count behavior. The breaker reason string MUST distinguish the two paths: signature-based trips start with `'diminishing returns (signature-based):'`; fallback trips start with `'diminishing returns (count fallback — finding signatures unavailable):'`. Reason: the platform consumes audit envelopes from multiple sources (live executor output, hand-edited fixtures, legacy or partial envelopes), and signature derivation can legitimately fail. Falling back to the legacy heuristic keeps the breaker functional in those cases; naming the fallback in the reason gives operators visibility into WHY a particular trip used count vs identity, so they can investigate envelope quality issues if they're getting count-based fallbacks unexpectedly. How to apply: any future signal-based check with a graceful-degradation path should follow the same pattern — name the path in the reason/output so observers can distinguish 'A tripped via primary' from 'A tripped via fallback because secondary signal was missing.' Silent fallback obscures upstream data-quality bugs.

title: Close-out — direct path; D001-D004 implemented as specified; SpinDine false-positive shape no longer trips
body: F001 shipped via direct path. compute_audit_finding_signature added to nested_orchestration.py as sibling of the F001 compute_finding_signature primitive (single platform notion of finding identity). check_diminishing_returns rewritten in circuit_breakers.py: signature path trips on persisted-set non-empty intersection across N=2 needs_changes rounds; fallback path replicates legacy count check when any finding lacks usable issue text, with the fallback fact named in the reason. Existing test_check_diminishing_returns updated to reflect contract change (same-issue rounds → signature-based trip; disjoint-issue rounds at same count → no trip); new test_check_diminishing_returns_signature_semantics covers the four operator-specified cases. Threshold DIMINISHING_RETURNS_MIN_ROUNDS remains constant (D003 — no operator knob). 2/2 targeted tests pass, 580 + 6 skipped full orchestrate suite (was 579 → +1 net), ruff clean, sanitization clean (565 files). The SpinDine plan 2026-05-01-001 false-positive shape (`auditor finding counts [3, 3] non-decreasing` with disjoint underlying findings) no longer trips under the new heuristic — verified by Case 2 of the new test. Plan closed.

title: Status-flip close-out — active → completed; cross-plan adjacency to stopped_no_progress recorded narrowly
body:
Tier 2/3 close-out warmup. D005 already recorded the impl-time close-out reasoning; this entry records the formal status-flip and the cross-plan context that did not exist when the impl-time memo was written.

Eight-step close-out executed: (1) `git ls-tree HEAD --` 4/4 tracked-vs-worktree match, no fallout, no untracked artifacts. (2) Validator clean before flip. (3) F001 passes:true; D001-D005 already in decisions.jsonl with schema {id, ts, by, title, body}; existing `evidence/closeout-memo.md` (plan-level, not per-feature) was written at impl-time and is precise about the diminishing-returns mechanism. Q1 sweep: zero closed-plan semantic citers (only mechanical validator-output dumps reference this plan name). Q2 classification: terminal status is implementation-result, not platform/runtime artifact — D005 says `Plan closed`, single feature `passes:true`, all tests green. (4) Plan-level memo: amended ONLY with a new section `Cross-plan context (added 2026-05-07 at status-flip close-out)` that records what this plan does NOT solve (the broader stopped_no_progress / timeout / stale-envelope class), what it DOES solve (signature-based intersection vs raw counts), and what remains a separate question (feature-defect vs environmental no-progress distinction). Impl-time memo content untouched. (5) D006 appended without reconstructing D001-D005. (6) `dontpanic plan close` exempt-flow path. (7) Re-validate clean. (8) Commit scoped to this plan dir.

Cross-plan adjacency recorded narrowly per operator framing: this plan fixes a `diminishing_returns` false-positive class (the count-based breaker, `circuit_breakers.check_diminishing_returns`). It does NOT solve the broader `stopped_no_progress` class observed at Phase A F003 close-out (Plan 2026-05-03-001 D009, closed `cb6d3cc`) and Phase B F002 close-out (Plan 2026-05-03-003 D012, closed `7ca7a23`). Those Phase A/B cases terminated `stopped_no_progress` — the verdict-based breaker (`circuit_breakers.check_no_progress`), which is unaffected by this plan. The two breakers are adjacent failure modes, not the same one. Whether to harden `stopped_no_progress` to distinguish feature-defect unchanged-verdict from environmental unchanged-verdict (auditor sandbox tempdir absence, stale-envelope from upstream timeout, etc.) remains a separate platform discussion; this plan does not implement that distinction, and the Phase B close-out memo's 'platform-shape signal worth tracking' line was correctly framed as adjacent, not subsumed by this work.

Narrative coherence improvement: closing this plan resolves the cross-plan stopped pattern table in Plan 2026-05-03-003's plan-level memo to 'one of the two adjacent breakers (count-based) has been fixed; the other (verdict-based) remains a queued but un-triggered platform discussion.' That is a more accurate characterization than 'separate discussion' alone, without overclaiming that this plan addresses both.

Reason: warmup target for Tier 2/3 batch — zero closed-plan semantic citers, single feature, deterministic acceptance, single-breaker scope. Establishes the eight-step + Q1/Q2 discipline for batches with more cross-plan surface to follow. Eight-step machinery stays warm; no cross-plan supersession or blocker semantics touched.
